Enquiry 1: Secret Code in Place-Names and Old Ordnance Survey Maps

Big Question: How do place-names and old maps unlock secret history on our doorstep?
Name: _______________________
Date: ________________________
KEY WORDS: Castra (Cas-tra) Domesday Book (Domes-day Book) Ordnance Survey (Ord-nance Sur-vey) Benchmark (Bench-mark) Trig Pillar (Trig Pil-lar)
TASK 1 Historical Evidence Detective • Inspect the Clue
Source A: Large-Scale 1880s Ordnance Survey Town Plan of Gloucester (1880s, Victorian Town Plan)
Map Clue: Dotted crosses marked '(Site of)' show vanished medieval churches, while 'B.M.' marks carved street benchmarks!

1a. Inspect Source A. How does comparing an 1880s Ordnance Survey map with a modern map reveal local change?

Starter: "Looking closely at Source A, comparing an 1880s Ordnance Survey map with a modern street map reveals change because..."
Word Bank: Ordnance Survey • 1880s • vanished • benchmarks
TASK 2 Chronology Challenge • Number These Events from 1 (Earliest) to 4 (Latest)
Ordnance Survey erects concrete hilltop triangulation ('trig') pillars across Britain (1936)
Roman legions build walled castra forts at Chester, Manchester, and Lancaster (AD 43–410)
Victorian Ordnance Survey teams publish detailed 1880s street plans and carve benchmarks (1880s)
King William I’s scribes record 13,000+ early place-names in the Domesday Book (AD 1086)

Enquiry 2: Reading Buildings on the High Street — Timber, Brick and Royal Cyphers

Big Question: How can timber frames, brickwork, and postboxes date a British street?
Name: _______________________
Date: ________________________
KEY WORDS: Jetty (Jet-ty) Sash Window (Sash Win-dow) Royal Cypher (Roy-al Cy-pher) Datestone (Date-stone) Ghost Sign (Ghost Sign)
TASK 1 Historical Evidence Detective • Inspect the Clue
Source A: Hexagonal Victorian "V.R." Penfold Cast-Iron Pillar Postbox (c. 1866–1879, Reign of Queen Victoria)
Cypher Clue: Postboxes keep their original monarch’s initials—V.R. (Victoria), G.R. (George), E.IIR (Elizabeth II), or C.IIIR (Charles III)!

1a. Inspect Source A and Source B. How do postboxes and datestones help date a British street?

Starter: "Looking closely at Source A and Source B, postboxes and carved datestones help date a street because..."
Word Bank: Royal Cypher • V.R. • datestone • 1874
TASK 2 Chronology Challenge • Number These Events from 1 (Earliest) to 4 (Latest)
Post Office repaints dark-green Victorian cast-iron pillar postboxes bright red (AD 1874)
Tudor carpenters frame overhanging oak 'jetty' houses with wattle and daub (1500s)
Railways carry machine-made red brick and terracotta to Victorian town halls (1880s–1890s)
Georgian architects build symmetrical stone terraces with sliding sash windows in Bath (1760s–1770s)

2b. Quick Explain: Which of these four events mattered most, and why?

Enquiry 3: Voices From Number 12 — Censuses, Parish Books and School Logbooks

Big Question: What can censuses, parish books, and school logbooks reveal about past families?
Name: _______________________
Date: ________________________
KEY WORDS: Census (Cen-sus) Enumerator (E-nu-mer-a-tor) Ostler (Ost-ler) Parish Register (Par-ish Reg-is-ter) School Logbook (School Log-book)
TASK 1 Historical Evidence Detective • Inspect the Clue
Source A: Handwritten 1881 Census Enumerator Page (Thistle Grove Lane, Chelsea)
Archive Clue: Linking the ten-year Census with 1538 Parish Registers and 1862 School Logbooks traces whole families across centuries!

1a. Inspect Source A. What can one 1881 Census page tell a detective about life on a Victorian street?

Starter: "Looking closely at Source A, a single 1881 Census page reveals rich clues about Victorian street life because..."
Word Bank: Census • enumerator • occupations • birthplaces
TASK 2 Chronology Challenge • Number These Events from 1 (Earliest) to 4 (Latest)
1921 UK Census household sheets open to public local history detectives after 100 years (AD 2022)
Parish churches in England and Wales begin keeping baptism, marriage, and burial registers (AD 1538)
Government rules require British headteachers to write weekly School Logbooks (AD 1862)
Britain holds its first national Census naming every person and occupation in each house (AD 1841)

2b. Quick Explain: Which of these four events mattered most, and why?

Enquiry 4: How Our Town Earned Its Living — Farms, Canals, Mills and Stations

Big Question: How do street names, canals, mills, and stations show past local work?
Name: _______________________
Date: ________________________
KEY WORDS: Turnpike (Turn-pike) Milestone (Mile-stone) Canal Lock (Ca-nal Lock) Aqueduct (Aq-ue-duct) Branch Line (Branch Line)
TASK 1 Historical Evidence Detective • Inspect the Clue
Source A: Carved Turnpike Stone Milestone and Horse Trough (Late 18th / Early 19th Century)
Transport Clue: Turnpike milestones served stagecoaches, while smooth canals let one horse pull thirty tonnes of heavy coal or china!

1a. Inspect Source A and Source B. Compare how turnpike roads and canals moved goods and travellers across Britain.

Starter: "Comparing Source A and Source B shows how turnpike roads and canals solved different transport problems because..."
Word Bank: milestones • turnpike • narrowboat • Canal Lock
TASK 2 Chronology Challenge • Number These Events from 1 (Earliest) to 4 (Latest)
Thousands of rural branch-line stations close and become walking trails after the Beeching Report (1960s)
Wymondham townspeople raise an octagonal timber Market Cross on open oak pillars (AD 1618)
Victorian steam railways connect market towns, ports, and red-brick stations across Britain (1840s)
Thomas Telford completes the cast-iron Pontcysyllte Canal Aqueduct for narrowboats (AD 1805)

2b. Quick Explain: Which of these four events mattered most, and why?

Enquiry 5: Names Carved in Stone — Local War Memorials and Commonwealth Records

Big Question: How can War Memorials and Commonwealth records trace one local soldier’s story?
Name: _______________________
Date: ________________________
KEY WORDS: War Memorial (War Me-mo-ri-al) Cenotaph (Cen-o-taph) Portland Stone (Port-land Stone) Regiment (Reg-i-ment) Memorial Plaque (Me-mo-ri-al Plaque)
TASK 1 Historical Evidence Detective • Inspect the Clue
Source A: Parish Church 1914–1918 War Memorial Tablet (Henham, Essex)
Equality Clue: Both CWGC white Portland stone headstones and bronze Memorial Plaques honoured officers and privates as equals!

1a. Inspect Source A and Source B. How did British communities and families remember loved ones buried overseas after 1918?

Starter: "Looking respectfully at Source A and Source B, families whose loved ones lay overseas remembered them at home through..."
Word Bank: War Memorial • surnames • Memorial Plaque • equals
TASK 2 Chronology Challenge • Number These Events from 1 (Earliest) to 4 (Latest)
Communities add 1939–1945 Rolls of Honour to local War Memorial crosses and church plaques (AD 1945+)
First World War breaks out and Fabian Ware begins recording soldiers’ battlefield graves (AD 1914)
Bereaved British villages and towns raise over 100,000 local War Memorials and receive bronze plaques (1919–1922)
Royal Charter establishes the War Graves Commission with equal white Portland stone headstones (May 1917)

2b. Quick Explain: Which of these four events mattered most, and why?

Enquiry 6: Living Memory, Oral History and Saving Local Heritage

Big Question: How do oral history, Blue Plaques, and trails protect local heritage today?
Name: _______________________
Date: ________________________
KEY WORDS: Oral History (O-ral His-to-ry) Decimal Day (Dec-i-mal Day) National Trust (Na-tion-al Trust) Blue Plaque (Blue Plaque) Listed Building (List-ed Build-ing)
TASK 1 Historical Evidence Detective • Inspect the Clue
Source A: English Heritage Ceramic Blue Plaque for Octavia Hill (1838–1912)
Conservation Clue: Pairing spoken oral history interviews with dated street photos gives both human warmth and exact dates!

1a. Inspect Source B and Source C. Why do good local historians combine oral history interviews with old street photographs?

Starter: "Good local historians combine recorded oral history interviews (Source C) with dated street photographs (Source B) because..."
Word Bank: Oral History • open questions • photographs • cross-check
TASK 2 Chronology Challenge • Number These Events from 1 (Earliest) to 4 (Latest)
Britain switches from pounds, shillings, and pence to 100 new pence on Decimal Day (15 February 1971)
London installs the world’s earliest ceramic historical Blue Plaques on famous homes (AD 1866)
Parliament passes the Town and Country Planning Act creating legally protected Listed Buildings (AD 1947)
Octavia Hill, Robert Hunter, and Hardwicke Rawnsley co-found the National Trust (January 1895)

2b. Quick Explain: Which of these four events mattered most, and why?
